Then room-identity, login-create-room, chatwoot-inbox, booking-picker, adgrant-content, dev-agents-kb, adgrant-generate and dev-agents. What is still running is in parcels.json, and it reuses ownership these released: booking-gate inherits the booking server and the dialog, and booking-linkedin inherits the identity layer.

the hosted connector-core.why: Four parcels in this programme call the hosted connector, and there is no the hosted connector code in the repository at all - a grep for it returns nothing. Whoever writes the second client writes a second error mapper, a second retry policy and a second opinion about where the key may live, and the third and fourth do it again. One client, first, alone, is the cheapest hour in the programme. It has no seams and no route: it is a module four other parcels import.
the hosted connector-core.done: One HTTP client for the whole the hosted connector surface, server-side only. Base URL is https://${HOSTED_WHATSAPP_DSN}/api/v1/... - the DSN carries host AND a non-standard port and differs per tenant, so api1 and 13111 appear nowhere in the code. Auth is the single header X-API-KEY, no Bearer prefix. The key authorises the ENTIRE the hosted connector workspace, not one account, so this directory must be unimportable from client code: read process.env at call time the way server/db.ts does, and add a test that fails if anything under client/ imports it. Errors: the RFC 7807 envelope in the brief section 1.2, mapped to a typed union keyed on `type`, with the enum values the brief lists. Retry 503 and 504 with backoff and NOTHING else; a 401 is an operator alert, never a retry - there is no Retry-After header and no documented quota anywhere, so the retry policy is ours and must be conservative. Missing env vars are not a crash and not a dead button: export an available() and an unavailableLine() the way server/waha.ts:89-115 does, so a caller can put one sentence on screen. Never log the key, never log a whole request body, and never let a hosted connector error string reach a visitor unfiltered - its `detail` can name our account. accounts.ts wraps GET /api/v1/accounts and GET /api/v1/accounts/{id} so the operator page can be told whether the two accounts in the brief section 4 are connected and what their sources[].status says (OK, STOPPED, ERROR, CREDENTIALS, PERMISSIONS, CONNECTING - a connected account can rot, and this is how we learn it did). Add both the hosted connector_ variables plus HOSTED_WHATSAPP_WEBHOOK_SECRET, HOSTED_WHATSAPP_CALENDAR_ACCOUNT_ID and HOSTED_WHATSAPP_WHATSAPP_ACCOUNT_ID to .env.example, each with one comment line saying what breaks without it. Tests inject fetch, as server/bridge/chatwoot.ts:57 does - no network in the suite. Do NOT build calendar, messaging or webhook calls here: three other parcels own those and each will import this one.

one call that ensures the webhook exists

the hosted connector-messaging.why: The owner asked for two things by name: create the webhook programmatically rather than by hand in a dashboard, and always check who a message is from, who it is to, and which chat it is in. Both are this parcel. It is also the transport two later parcels stand on - the booking confirmation and the room's WhatsApp route both send and receive through it - so it is built before either and knows about neither.
the hosted connector-messaging.done: Send, receive, and the webhook's own lifecycle. SENDING: both send routes are multipart/form-data, NOT JSON, and that is the biggest single difference from WAHA - the brief section 1.5 has the field lists. POST /api/v1/chats is documented as creating a chat if needed or using an existing one, so it is the single upsert send path; pass account_id on it as a safety rail. THE WEBHOOK, IN CODE: at route registration, GET /api/v1/webhooks, find ours by request_url, create it only when absent - idempotent, never a second one - and delete ones pointing at hosts we have retired. The address is ours to compute, ${PUBLIC_BASE_URL}/api/the hosted connector/inbound, which is why the owner sets no URL anywhere; HOSTED_WHATSAPP_WEBHOOK_SECRET is a random string, not an address. REGISTER TWO, and there is no third: the hosted connector has five webhook types and a calendar is not among them, so the calendar is polled and never pushed. One is source: messaging. The other is the account-lifecycle one, because a linked WhatsApp device can be logged out from the phone, and the difference between learning that from a webhook and discovering it from a silent send failure is a day of a room looking broken. The exact source value for account status is NOT in the webhooks page - read https://developer.the hosted connector.com/docs/account-lifecycle and use the value that page gives. Do not guess it: a webhook registered with an invalid source is one that silently never fires, and you would report success. Both webhooks point at our one endpoint and carry the same secret, and the handler branches on the payload - an account-status event is not a message and must not reach the message path. Two documented gotchas that both fail SILENTLY and must both be handled: a webhook created by API carries no Content-Type header by default, so pass headers: [{key: Content-Type, value: application/json}] or express.json() leaves req.body empty; and there is no HMAC signature anywhere in the hosted connector, only a shared secret in a header you name, so use HOSTED_WHATSAPP_WEBHOOK_SECRET compared with timingSafeEqual. server/identity.ts:466-474 shows the shape and ALSO shows the bug - when its env var is unset the check passes. Here, no secret configured means the endpoint refuses everything. Do not copy that line. THE INBOUND RULE, which is this parcel's real subject: the brief's seven checks, each its own named exported function with its own test. (1) the secret matches. (2) account_id is on an allowlist of accounts we operate, not merely present. (3) sender.attendee_provider_id !== account_info.user_id - our own sent messages arrive as message_received too and there is NO fromMe flag, so without this the room echoes our own agents back as if the visitor said it. (4) chat_id is present and is the chat expected for whatever this answers. (5) message_id has not been seen - five retries are guaranteed on any non-200 within 30s, so idempotency is not optional. (6) event === message_received; the other five events are not messages. (7) timestamp is recent, because a reconnect delivers a burst from the disconnected period. Anything failing a check is recorded and dropped, never guessed at. The body field is `message`, a string - the REST API calls it `text`, and that mismatch is a bug waiting. Reply 200 in well under 30s and do the work after. IDENTITY: attendee_provider_id is a TAGGED UNION, either <phone>@s.whatsapp.net or <id>@lid, and the second form carries no number. Model it as a union and never regex it for digits: WhatsApp's LID migration is real, the hosted connector's own docs contradict themselves about which form is internal, and the hosted connector has no LID resolver where WAHA has one. Report that in your handoff. Contact reads are GET /api/v1/chats/{chat_id}/attendees and GET /api/v1/chat_attendees/{id}: you get name (a self-set push name, display only), picture_url and provider_id, and there is no phone field and no WhatsApp branch of specifics. This parcel does not touch server/identity.ts or server/waha.ts - room-identity owns that swap and will import you.

adgrant-front.done: A new AdGrant.AI front page and shell, in this application, at its own route tree - NOT on a second host, and the reason is in the frozen list: client/index.html carries the one head this application serves, so a second site with its own title and meta cannot be done without editing a frozen file. That switch is owner work for when no wave is running. So build it so it CAN move: no import of the top-rated.team header or footer, its own chrome, and nothing that assumes the apex. Extend that deliberately rather than starting a new palette. ADGRANT_LIBRARY at :17-27 already names the five sections of the live site with a line each and links them without copying them: keep that discipline. THE 74 LIBRARY PAGES STAY WHERE THEY ARE and are linked. Moving them is a separate programme, and breaking 74 indexed URLs in order to redesign a front page would be the most expensive kind of tidy. data/kb/kb.adgrant-ai.json is our own written material on this product and data/kb/kb.ad-grants.json is Google's own documentation of the programme; both are already built, and the eligibility and policy facts in the second are the ones this page must not get wrong - a nonprofit reading a wrong eligibility line loses a grant worth 10k a month. client/src/components/workspace/AdGrantPanel.tsx and AD_GRANT_SETUP are the setup this product actually performs, in order; describe that rather than a feature list. FIX WHAT THE LIVE SITE GETS WRONG rather than reproducing it: real type in two faces, not twenty-eight; no pinch-zoom lock; and no machine-translation gadget standing in for localisation - English only is an honest state and a googtrans cookie is not. The page ends in a room: the ad-grants door already exists with its own agent and corpus, so the action is to open a room on this product, not a contact form. Set the page's own title and description the way client/src/pages/landing.tsx does, in the page, since the shell's are not yours to edit. data/build-shots/adgrant-ai.png is a screenshot of the OLD site, shown on a builds card here - say in your handoff that it needs replacing, and do not replace it yourself.

booking-server.why: Booking is Google's own overlay today: a third-party script, a 1x1 clipped host div, and a hidden button we click. It works, and it means the visitor leaves our page into Google's UI, we learn nothing about the booking, and the availability logic is Google's. This is the server half of replacing it. It exists before the popup so the popup has something true to talk to, and both build to the shapes the brief fixes in writing.
booking-server.done: GET /api/booking/slots, POST /api/booking and GET /api/booking/confirmed, exactly as the brief section 3 specifies them - those shapes are a contract with a parcel running in the same wave and may not drift. THERE IS NO FREE/BUSY ENDPOINT IN the hosted connector: seven calendar routes exist and none of them is availability, so we compute it. Read the primary calendar ONCE (GET /api/v1/calendars, take is_primary, assert is_read_only === false, keep its id and its own timezone) and cache it - not per widget load. Then list events over a window PADDED BY A DAY ON EACH SIDE with expand_recurring=true, and do the overlap test yourself. Three traps, each of which silently shows a busy day as free, and each needs a test with a fixture that fails without it. (1) An all-day event is {date} with NO date_time, so new Date(ev.start.date_time) is Invalid Date on the owner's holiday and the week reads as open - branch on "date" in ev.start and treat it as busy for the whole date in the calendar's zone. (2) start and end are CONTAINMENT filters: the docs say starting-after and ending-before, so a 09:00-10:00 event is excluded from a 09:30-11:00 query while still blocking it. That is why the window is padded and the real test is ours. (3) Without expand_recurring a weekly standup arrives as one master event with an RRULE array and is invisible to the calculation. Do not trust the undocumented busy=true alone: filter on is_cancelled !== true AND transparency !== transparent AND an event_type not in a declined/birthday set, so the rule is readable and testable rather than a server-side interpretation nobody documented. Cache the computed window server-side for 30-60s; never one the hosted connector call per rendered calendar cell. WRITING THE BOOKING: POST the event with transparency: opaque, conference: {provider: google_meet} and no url (which auto-provisions the Meet link), and notify: true - notify DEFAULTS TO FALSE, and without it the visitor never gets an invite, which is the whole reason we are not connecting their calendar. The 201 returns only {event_id}, not the event, so GET it back if you want the Meet URL. TWO THINGS THE DOCS DO NOT SETTLE, and you must settle them by experiment rather than by guess, then write what you found into your handoff: whether attendees: [] satisfies the required constraint (schema-valid, untested - fall back to the visitor's own address, which we collect, or to dan@top-rated.team), and whether date_time must be UTC-with-Z while time_zone is advisory (the docs say ISO 8601 UTC datetime AND carry a separate time_zone field, which is contradictory). Send both, then read the created event out of Google Calendar and confirm the real hour before you report done - a booking widget that is an hour out is worse than none. code.ts mints the planted WhatsApp code: the alphabet at server/identity.ts:98-102, with no dash, underscore, I, O, 0 or 1, because it gets dictated - a nanoid with dashes once broke about 40% of binds and the comment there records it. Export the regex so the handler and the test share one pattern. Five-minute expiry, and /confirmed reads it back. Register a matcher with server/the hosted connector/inbound.ts rather than parsing a webhook yourself: the seven checks belong to one parcel. email is the ONLY optional field; without it the event is still created and invited is false, and a placeholder address built from a phone number is permitted only where there IS a number and must never be reported to the visitor as an invite that will arrive. Do NOT build visitor-calendar connection: the brief section 2.3 prices it and refuses it.

booking-dialog.why: The owner asked for our own booking popup in our own style. The trap is the call sites: there are SEVENTEEN book-a-call anchors in eleven files, plus a slash command in the room, plus a hardcoded link in the frozen index.html. A parcel that edits seventeen call sites collides with every other parcel in its wave and several in the next. So this one changes what the hook DOES and not what it RETURNS, and touches no call site at all.
booking-dialog.done: Our popup, opened by the same useBooking() the site already spreads. THE CONTRACT THAT MAY NOT CHANGE: useBooking() returns exactly { onClick, onMouseEnter, onFocus } (client/src/hooks/use-booking.ts:75), spread as {...booking} at seventeen sites. Keep all three keys and their meanings. Warming stays: a module-level one-shot listener on the first pointerdown, touchstart, keydown or scroll anywhere on the page, because there is no hover on a phone and touchstart is only about 50ms ahead of click - the reasoning at :16-27 still holds, only now it warms a slots fetch instead of Google's script. The modifier-key and middle-click bail-outs at :53-62 stay exactly as they are: a cmd-click must still open a tab. WHAT INVERTS: today the href is a real fallback because a third-party script can be blocked, so preventDefault is conditional. Now the popup is ours, so preventDefault becomes unconditional on a plain left click - but the href STAYS as the no-JS path, and target=_blank comes off nothing. Delete bookingReady(), which is exported with no caller anywhere in the tree. THE POPUP: lazily imported with the exact incantation the five LeadDialog hosts use (client/src/components/site/Header.tsx:10 and four others). The reason is stated there - LeadDialog pulls in Radix and the header is in the landing chunk paid traffic downloads first - and a second eager Radix dialog regresses it. Match LeadDialog's Radix usage, its focus and Escape handling, its light and dark treatment, and the site's own type and colour tokens. There is no ui/dialog wrapper in use: grep proves it has no importer, so import Radix directly as LeadDialog does. Read GET /api/booking/slots and POST /api/booking exactly as the brief section 3 fixes them; that is a contract with a parcel in your own wave. Slots arrive as local wall-clock times in a named timezone, which is what a human picks - print the timezone beside them, because a visitor in another country booking a 14:00 needs to know whose 14:00 it is. A day with no slots is present and empty: say nothing is free rather than hiding the day. ONE optional field, email, with a sentence saying what it buys (a real calendar invite) and what its absence costs (nothing else). A 409 is not an error to swallow: the response carries fresh availability, so redraw with it and say the time was just taken. On a phone, the save button opens the WhatsApp deep link from the response and then polls GET /api/booking/confirmed, so the confirmation lands in the popup the visitor came from as well as in WhatsApp; on a desktop the same button just confirms. THE ROOM'S SLASH COMMAND: client/src/components/workspace/Composer.tsx:220-228 bypasses the hook because a slash command has no click to fall through, and its comment says so. Give it an imperative open that resolves without an event, and leave its window.open fallback working. THE ASKWIDGET COMPOSITION MUST SURVIVE: three anchors at AskWidget.tsx:449, :477 and :539 spread {...booking} BEFORE a local onClick that calls onAskedForAPerson?.() and then booking.onClick(event). Both orders are load-bearing and both are recorded there as bugs that already happened: the JSX order because spreading after replaces the handler and loses the signal, the runtime order because booking.onClick may navigate and a signal recorded after navigation is never recorded. You are changing what booking.onClick does, so read those three sites and verify the signal still fires first.

room-identity.why: Three of the owner's asks are one feature: let a room's owner name it, let a room be claimed so it is theirs, and make that survive a deploy. Today a room's name is written once at the instant of creation and is immutable through every interface this product has - four independent checks confirm it, including a grep for renameWorkspace that returns nothing - and the identity bindings that would say who owns a room live in a new Map() that empties on restart. Alone in its wave because it writes into the room, the storage layer and the identity layer, and everything reads those.
room-identity.done: A room that can be named by whoever owns it, and an ownership that survives a deploy. THE TABLE: a new table in shared/schema-rooms.ts, re-exported from shared/schema.ts in ONE line - drizzle-kit follows the export, and fifteen lines in a seam do not merge. It holds what server/identity.ts:109-116 already models - workspaceId, provider, providerId, displayName, boundAt - and the first binding on a room is its owner. Persist through server/identity-store.ts, so server/identity.ts stops being the store as well as the logic, and keep the in-memory path as the fallback when there is no database. THERE IS NO DATABASE ON THE DEPLOYMENT TODAY: DATABASE_URL is unset, rooms live in memory, and every deploy destroys them. A claim written to a table that does not exist is the bug the owner already reported. Say so in your handoff, plainly, as the thing that blocks this feature from meaning anything - do not quietly ship it and call it done. THE NAME: add a rename to the Storage interface (server/storage.ts:82-93 - nine writes and a touch, none of which updates a workspace), implemented in BOTH MemoryStorage and PgStorage and wired through the delegating object; an updateWorkspaceSchema beside the createWorkspaceSchema that already caps a name at 120; a PATCH route; and a ServerEvent so other people in the room see the new name without reloading - server/ws.ts is how state reaches them. Only the owner may rename. An unclaimed room has no owner, so the control appears once a claim exists, and a room nobody has claimed keeps the name roomName() gave it. THE CONTROL, and the standing instruction is DO NOT COMPLICATE THE ROOM: the name is already on screen in three places (WorkspaceSidebar.tsx:153-155, the desktop top bar at workspace.tsx:187-191, and the owner's lead notifications), and the smallest honest affordance is to make the one the owner already reads editable in place. No new panel, no settings screen, no modal for one text field. IDENTITY, AND THIS DECISION IS ALREADY MADE: LinkedIn stays on the official Sign In with LinkedIn (OIDC), which is built, tested and correct. The brief section 2.1 prices the alternative and refuses it; the short version is that the hosted connector hosted auth would bill EUR 5 per claimed room per month - more than the entire AI budget of the room it identifies - and would ask the visitor for their LinkedIn PASSWORD on a third-party page that may present a captcha. Do not switch it. Leave the scope at openid profile: adding email is a review cost, not a free upgrade. WHATSAPP: swap the transport from WAHA to server/the hosted connector/messaging.ts, for OUR OWN NUMBER ONLY. WAHA does exactly two jobs - probeWaha() at server/waha.ts:89-115 learns our own number so the wa.me link has a destination, and an inbound webhook delivers the reply - and the hosted connector does both for one account at no per-visitor cost. What the VISITOR does must not change: they tap a wa.me link and message us. That direction is also the safe one - the hosted connector's own provider limits say a fresh account can be blocked after two or three new outbound chats, while replying to inbound is effectively unlimited. Keep the sha256(pepper, chatId) identifier at :387-389: a phone number is never stored and never logged. Keep the dictatable nonce alphabet and BIND_CODE_RE. Keep binding as an allowance rather than a gate - allowanceForWorkspace() at :164-179 gives a bound room three times the turns and budget, and the room address stays a bearer credential. AND KEEP THE THIRD ROUTE the owner asked for: we do not know a person's WhatsApp, so adding a number to a room by hand must remain possible and must not be dressed up as verification. A number somebody typed is a note; a number that messaged us is a proof; the room must not print them the same way. RoomIdentityDialog is the popup a newly created room shows to offer the claim - login-create-room opens it from the site in the next wave, and you do not need to know how.

login-create-room.why: The owner wants the Open-a-room links on the site to become one control doing both halves of the same job: get back into a room you already have, or start a new one and be offered ownership of it. The list of rooms this browser remembers already exists and is already maintained - twelve of them, newest first, in localStorage - and /w with no token already renders it. What is missing is that the list is reachable only from an address nobody types.
login-create-room.done: One control where Open a room is now, reading a list that already exists. THE LIST IS NOT NEW: listStoredWorkspaces() in client/src/hooks/use-workspace.ts:48-58 returns the remembered rooms newest first and returns [] rather than throwing in private mode; rememberWorkspace() keeps the last twelve; client/src/App.tsx:51 already routes /w with no token to them. Present that list; do not build a second store. And do not import the room's chunk to do it - the site's landing chunk is what paid traffic downloads and the workspace bundle is 198KB of it. Either export the reader from somewhere the site can import without pulling the room in, or read localStorage directly behind the same try/catch guard. THE CONTROL: two actions fused into one, as the owner described - the left half returns you to a room, the right half makes one. Hover opens the list on a pointer device; on a phone there is no hover, so the return half opens it on tap and the create half creates. A browser that remembers no room must not show an empty menu: with nothing to return to, the control is only the create action, and it says so. Every entry needs its name, and this is where the owner's other complaint lands - he saw three rooms all called Conversion tracking, because the name was a hardcoded fallback. server/storage.ts:264-272 fixed the fallback and room-identity makes the name editable; the menu shows whatever a room is called plus when it was last seen, so two rooms from the same door are still tellable apart. CREATE: use-open-room.ts already stamps the general-room source and navigates to /w/:token; after it lands, the room offers the claim through the dialog room-identity built in the previous wave. Do not build a second claim UI, and do not put the claim in the site's chunk. THE CALL SITES YOU OWN, and they are why this parcel is late in the programme: Header.tsx (desktop nav and the phone burger), FirstScreen.tsx (the hero, where OPEN A ROOM currently comes first, before BOOK A CALL), doors.tsx and door.tsx (each door's hero and its panel band). Keep the order the owner established - the room action first, then Book a call, then Leave a message - and keep the capitalisation he asked for. On a door, the room opened must still be that door's room and not the general one: the source stamp is what decides that, and it is easy to lose while moving a button. Nothing here may change what a booking anchor does. booking-dialog owns the hook, and you own some of the files its anchors sit in, so leave every {...booking} spread and every href exactly as you found it - including the three composed onClick handlers around AskWidget.

chatwoot-inbox.why: The owner wants contractors to answer a room from ChatWoot. Most of that is built and none of it is reachable: 139 lines of client, 756 of orchestration, 210 of attribution and 466 of tests exist, and BridgePanel is imported nowhere - data/builds/top-rated-team.json:30 records that as deliberate, so nothing on the site claims a bridge the room does not offer. What is actually missing is two things: the panel is not mounted, and the design asks the owner to paste one conversation id per room, which does not scale past him doing it by hand.
chatwoot-inbox.done: A room that can talk to ChatWoot without anybody pasting an id, and a panel a person can reach. FIRST, THE CONSTITUTION: docs/parcels-programme-1.json:329-350 is the parcel that specified this bridge, and its done text still binds. Attribution is the whole job and the rest is plumbing. Every outbound message names its speaker from the room's member record, not from whoever typed. An agent's message must never arrive looking like a person's. An unmappable inbound sender is marked unattributed, never guessed. A bridged agent turn claims through server/spend.ts, because there is prior art of an unguarded endpoint being hit for five hours. THE ROOM TOKEN NEVER APPEARS IN AN OUTBOUND PAYLOAD. A delivery failure surfaces on the message, not in a log. Contradict none of it. THE CHANGE: today server/bridge/chatwoot.ts:55-91 speaks the application API - POST /api/v1/accounts/{accountId}/conversations/{conversationId}/messages with an api_access_token - which is right for speaking as an agent into one conversation the owner found by hand, and wrong for a room that should make its own. Add the API-Inbox client path, so a room creates its own contact and its own conversation in an inbox keyed by inbox_identifier and contact_identifier, and keep the agent path for what it is good at. Correlate a conversation to a room the way index.ts:91 already does, by an accountId-and-conversationId key, and carry the room's identity in ChatWoot custom attributes rather than in message text - the token must not travel. FOUR EXISTING WEAKNESSES TO FIX WHILE YOU ARE IN HERE, each verified in the code. (1) Echo suppression at chatwoot.ts:128 tests only for agent_bot and private, not for message_type === outgoing, which is exactly what our own API-sent message comes back as, so our messages can loop. (2) The dedupe key at index.ts:260-269 is the first 80 characters of the body with a 30-minute TTL, so two genuine thanks half an hour apart collapse into one. (3) Webhook auth at index.ts:240-252 RETURNS TRUE WHEN NO ENV VAR IS SET - an open webhook by default, which must become a refusal. (4) The whole bridge map is in process memory by design (index.ts:10-12, a restart forgets every bridge), which is honest but must be said on screen where a person connects one. MOUNT THE PANEL, and the standing instruction is not to complicate the room: it is plumbing, it belongs where a room's other plumbing lives, and it must be invisible to a visitor who has no bridge. A panel that is empty for everyone except the owner does not belong on the first screen.

booking-picker.why: The booking popup works and the owner does not like how it asks for a date. It is a vertical list of days, each with its own row of times folded underneath, so choosing a Thursday afternoon means scrolling past Monday, Tuesday and Wednesday. He wants it horizontal: pick the day of a month in one place, pick the time beside it or under it. This parcel changes only that, and only in the one file.
booking-picker.done: A two-pane picker. On a wide screen: a month grid of days on the left, and the times for the selected day on the right. On a phone the same two panes stack, grid above times, because a 7-column grid and a column of times side by side at 375px is neither. Nothing else about the popup changes - not the email field, not the WhatsApp deep link, not the polling, not the 409 redraw, not the expired-code retry. FOUR THINGS THAT ARE ALREADY RIGHT AND MUST SURVIVE. (1) A day with nothing free is PRESENT with an empty array, at four layers, and each layer is pinned: server/booking/slots.ts:261 pushes the day outside the weekend guard and says why at :11-12; server/booking/slots.test.ts:238-264 asserts fourteen days come back and that a Saturday's slots deep-equal []; client/src/lib/booking.ts:169-185 copies it through, pinned at client/src/lib/booking.test.ts:114-120; and the dialog prints a sentence. Keep the sentence. A grid that silently omits a day is a worse answer than one that says nothing is free. (2) The timezone is stated beside the times, because a visitor in another country booking a 14:00 needs to know whose 14:00 it is. (3) firstDayWithASlot falls back to days[0] when EVERY day is empty, which leaves a date selected, no time, and the submit disabled - correct but silent. Say something in that case: nothing free in this window. (4) The 409 response carries fresh availability and redraws. adgrant-setup-files.why: A starter template page today prints seven counts and hands over nothing. The owner's point is that a template IS the setup: the person reading it wants the files, not the arithmetic. The live product already has them — /api/templates/<slug> returns the whole structure, 14KB of campaigns, ad groups, keywords, sitelinks, callouts and snippets — and our build fetches only the list endpoint, which omits it. So the data exists, the CSV writer exists, and nothing joins them.
adgrant-setup-files.done: A TEMPLATE PAGE HANDS OVER ITS SETUP FILES, including the single one Google Ads Editor imports. Four things are known and each one is a trap if you find it late. (1) THE STRUCTURE IS ALREADY PUBLISHED but not at the endpoint we use: `/api/templates` omits it and `/api/templates/<slug>` returns it. Fetch per template in scripts/build-adgrant.ts. (2) IT IS NOT OUR SHAPE. The live template structure is {callouts, campaigns[{name, status, dailyBudget, adGroups}], languageCodes, languageIds, locationIds, locationList, sitelinks, structuredSnippets, totalDailyBudget}. structureToEditorCsv in server/adgrant/generate.ts takes AdGrantAccountStructure, which has authorisedDomain, per-campaign bidStrategy and per-campaign sitelinks. Map one to the other deliberately and test the mapping; do not widen the CSV writer until it accepts anything, because it is the file somebody imports into a live Google Ads account. (3) DO NOT PUT TWELVE STRUCTURES IN THE CLIENT BUNDLE. shared/adgrant.ts is imported by the landing page; twelve 14KB structures is about 170KB of JavaScript for a page that shows seven numbers. The structures belong behind a route, fetched when the visitor asks for the files, which is also what makes it "the result of a submit" rather than a page weight. (4) THE FILE IS THE PRODUCT AND IT MUST BE HONEST: a CSV that imports cleanly and does nothing is worse than none. Every campaign it writes is Paused, as the generator's already are, and the page says so before the download rather than after. WHAT MUST NOT CHANGE: nothing is written into anybody's Google Ads account by this parcel — that is the next one — and the page keeps saying so.
